summary: Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Gori, Labrang, Drepung, Guru, and Detsha monasteries under numerous teachers. He served as Dean of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956) and President of the Buddhist Association of China (~1953–1966).

Sherry B. Ortner (born 1941) works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan, and held posts at Sarah Lawrence College (~1971–1977), University of Michigan (~1977–1994), and UCLA (~2004).
Sherry Chayat (born 1943) is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Vassar College and under traditional teacher Eido Shimano.

Shi Hu (1891–1962) was a philosopher, sinologist, and historian. Educated at Cornell, National University, Teachers College, and Columbia under John Dewey, he held posts at Peking University (~1917–1948), Fu Jen Catholic University, and Academia Sinica (1958–1962).
Shi Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where he studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2016).

Shichang Ma (born 1938) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and archaeology. He served as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka (1904–1987) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1925 to 1928 and later held a post there from ~1949 to 1968.

Shigeki Moro (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and computational fields. Educated at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, he held posts at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and Waseda University (professor, 2025).
Shigemasa Fukui (born 1935) is a sinologist and historian. He studied at Waseda University (~1954–1958) and served as a professor there from ~1978 to 2005.

Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied under Seiichiro Ono at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University, and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).
Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested 1999 and 2017).

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa and the University of Tokyo under Kodo Sawaki. He held professorial posts at Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Shigeo Yokoyama (born 1954) works in religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1973–1983) and held posts at Okayama University and Nara Women's University (~2002–2019).

Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Tokyo and Kyoto universities, he held positions at Kyoto Normal School, Koyasan University, Otani University (1955–1978), Ryukoku University, and the Japanese Institute of Religious Folklore.
Shigeru Kato (1880–1946) was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1906) and later held a post there from ~1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1967), and later held posts at Tenri University and the University of the Sacred Heart.
Shih-Hsiang Chen (1912–1971) was a sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1931–1935). He held an academic post at the University of California, Berkeley, from ~1945 to 1971.
Shikaripur N. Sridhar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at Stony Brook University as Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026).
Shikazo Mori (1906–1980) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1927 to 1930 and held a post at Bukkyo University from ~1970 to 1978.

Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at China Inner Studies College under Jian Ouyang (1920). He held posts at Boone University (~1920–1922), Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1937–1938).
